03The investment

Luxury hotels are investing heavily in wellness. But guests who’ve crossed time zones are often too exhausted from travelling to enjoy it, and don’t know what to use, and when, to feel better.

Why it stays that way

Wellness usually sits with a director responsible for the department’s operational and financial direction: the team, the standards, the budget.

Timing it to each guest’s journey means connecting the rooms, the food, the spa and the gym, which sit across different departments, so currently no one owns it across the hotel.

That’s what ALT‑15° does, using AI and circadian rhythm science, personalised and bespoke to each guest.

06The commercial case

When every luxury hotel can buy the same wellness inventory, owning it stops being a reason to choose you.

For a guest who’s crossed time zones, wellness means recovery.

Today: amenities to list
  • Spa and treatments
  • Gym and recovery suite
  • Sleep and room environment
  • Restaurants and room service
And decisions to make

What to eat, which treatment and whether there’s time for one, what exercise to do and whether to visit the gym at all. Every choice is left to a guest already emotionally drained and low on energy from the journey, with jet lag compounding both.

77% of long-haul travellers say jet lag affects their concentration.*

→
With Travel Performance: an offer to sell

We time light, food, movement, sleep and treatments to each guest’s journey, so every service your hotel already offers works with their circadian rhythm, not against it.

These are departments you already run, and once they’re timed to the guest, they become reasons to book, spend and return.

Decisions eliminated

Before they arrive, each guest receives a recommended plan for the whole stay, timed to their body clock: when to eat, when to train, when to recover and when to sleep. Every service is offered at the right time for them, so there’s nothing left to decide or figure out. That peace of mind has a price, and it’s yours to sell.

*Source: Kayak and Airbus survey of 1,000 UK long-haul travellers, 2016

09What the hotel already knows

The flight number isn’t just data. It’s the start of the guest experience.

Whether a guest has crossed one time zone or eight, most hotels look
after them in exactly the same way.

01  Already in the booking
  • Where they’ve come from
  • How many time zones they’ve crossed
  • How long they’ve been travelling
  • What time it is for their body on arrival
02  A short questionnaire before arrival

Sent with the booking confirmation: whether they’re a morning or evening person and the purpose of the trip.

03  A bespoke plan for each guest

Emailed before arrival: when to eat, train, recover and sleep across the stay.
They can accept or change any part of it, and the hotel has everything arranged and ready for when they arrive.
